paragraphs.text: Meeting URU-10-01 occurred at Uruapan on 2010-11-18. A former laboratory worker reported secondhand on a gathering of avocado growers in Uruapan that the source believed included representatives of the new highland network. The source could not name any participant and acknowledged that the gathering was a regular growers' association meeting at which the price of fruit and the cost of trucking were the only topics the source's contact could recall. The reporting office treats the account as background on the agricultural economy in which the network operates.

The source described Uruapan during the period as a town where the fruit trade dominates every conversation and where trucking contracts are the main form of patronage. The source stated that growers were complaining about fees charged on the roads into the Tierra Caliente by armed men whose affiliation was unclear. The source had no information suggesting that the growers' meeting was used for anything other than its stated purpose. The source added that the association's trucking contracts are awarded by a committee whose members are themselves growers, and that the armed men on the roads had begun approaching committee members directly. The source could not say whether any contract had yet been awarded under pressure.

The reporting office assesses this as background on the regional economy rather than as information on a specific network. The source's access is historical and secondhand. The account is retained because the road fees mentioned by the growers may indicate the beginning of territorial control in the hill country. The reporting office will compare this reporting with later accounts from the same district.
